facts.text: Union City was founded in 1800 as Miles Mills, named after William Miles who built a dam and mills on French Creek.
In 1858 the Philadelphia and Erie Railroad arrived, turning Union City into a rail hub for the burgeoning oil industry.
The town’s barrel‑making industry grew after 1870, producing the nation’s largest oil barrels and shaping its economy for generations.
A devastating fire in 1879 destroyed most Main Street businesses, but brick rebuilds emerged, giving the historic district its distinctive 19th‑century look.
Union City’s historic district earned National Register status in 1990, preserving over a century of architecture and local heritage.
The Union City Historical Society Museum, a three‑story Main Street landmark, showcases a diverse collection that reflects the town’s rural roots and industrial past.
